transcription_method: Manual transcription from the supplied course specification text. Light spelling, punctuation and whitespace normalization only. Related sub-points remain grouped where the source presents them as one ILO; topic headings and assessment descriptions are not relabelled as outcomes. No external clinical content has been added.
scope_note: Granular transcription of the knowledge ILOs (printed pages 3–11), psychomotor ILOs (printed pages 12–16), and PBL/seminar/TBL ILOs plus research project ILOs (printed page 17) for SI 2.4.2. The separate topic headings are not counted as ILOs. This is not faculty-verified.

outcomes.transcribed_text: Define shock, classify shock and describe its clinical presentations.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of shock, including complications and mechanisms of irreversible shock.
Define haemostasis and explain its mechanisms.
Explain causes, pathogenesis, types and management of haemorrhage.
Summarize causes, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of common coagulopathies.
Illustrate indications, precautions and complications of blood transfusion.
Discuss fluid and electrolyte balance and imbalance.
Discuss acid-base balance and imbalance.
Discuss anabolic and catabolic states of the surgical patient and causes, pathogenesis and management of short-bowel syndrome.
Outline enteral and parenteral nutrition principles, types, indications, contraindications, benefits and complications.
Classify specific and non-specific surgical infections.
Explain clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of specific and non-specific surgical infections.
Analyse antibiotic-therapy principles, types, administration policies and antimicrobial resistance.
Classify neoplasms and describe their pathogenesis, diagnosis, grading, spread and common malignant presentations.
Outline indications, limitations and principles of organ transplantation and summarize common surgical transplantation techniques.
Identify stem-cell therapy and explain recent expectations of stem-cell therapy in surgery.
Define dysphagia, formulate its differential diagnosis and plan management.
Discuss causes, clinical presentations and management of achalasia.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and reflux oesophagitis.
Explain types, causes, diagnosis and management of hiatus hernia.
Outline pathogenesis and management of corrosive oesophageal stricture, oesophageal foreign body and oesophageal trauma.
Discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, classification, diagnosis and management of oesophageal cancer.
Define oesophageal replacement surgery and describe its indications, common techniques and complications.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnosis, complications and management of peptic ulcer disease.
Formulate classifications of gastric neoplasms.
Discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of gastric carcinoma.
Summarize common gastrectomy techniques and post-gastrectomy complications.
Define morbid obesity and list its complications and indications for bariatric surgery.
Explain multidisciplinary approaches to management of patients with morbid obesity.
Outline bariatric procedures, including indications, techniques, side effects, complications and limitations.
Discuss surgical management of inflammatory bowel disease.
Discuss causes, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of intestinal diverticular disease and intestinal vascular disease.
Discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, pathology, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of small-bowel tumours.
Discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, clinical presentations, classifications, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of colonic tumours.
Outline causes and types of gastrointestinal trauma, fistulae and stomas.
Explain management of gastrointestinal fistulae.
Discuss pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnosis, differential diagnosis and management of appendicitis.
Discuss pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of appendiceal neoplasms.
Demonstrate indications, techniques and complications of appendectomy.
Describe anorectal problems including fissure, haemorrhoids, prolapse, perianal abscess and perianal fistula.
Discuss clinical presentations, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of common anorectal problems.
Discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of anorectal tumours and outline causes, diagnosis and management of faecal incontinence.
Illustrate surgical anatomy of the hepatobiliary region.
Outline causes, classification and management of liver trauma.
Formulate classifications of neoplastic liver lesions and list their incidence, risk factors and causes.
Plan management of focal liver lesions and formulate differential diagnoses of neoplastic and non-neoplastic liver lesions.
Explain pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnostic procedures and management approaches for neoplastic liver lesions; discuss diagnosis and management of liver metastases.
List indications and types of hepatic resection and identify causes of portal hypertension.
Explain pathogenesis, clinical presentations and management of portal hypertension.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, clinical presentations and management of benign gallbladder disease and incidence, risk factors, causes, diagnosis and management of gallbladder carcinoma.
Illustrate indications and different techniques of cholecystectomy and outline post-cholecystectomy complications.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnostic procedures and management of pancreatitis.
Outline causes, classification, diagnosis and management of pancreatic trauma, pancreatic fistulae and pancreatic pseudocyst.
Identify incidence, risk factors and causes of pancreatic carcinoma; explain its pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnostic procedures and management.
List pancreatic endocrine tumours and discuss incidence, site, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management.
Discuss diagnosis and management of gastric and intestinal lymphoma and gastrointestinal stromal tumour.
Describe incidence, types, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of congenital splenic diseases, splenic infarction, infection, trauma and tumours.
List causes of hypersplenism and splenomegaly; demonstrate indications and techniques of splenectomy and outline its complications.
Discuss incidence, causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of thyroglossal cyst, thyroglossal fistula and ectopic thyroid tissue.
Formulate differential diagnoses of goitre and discuss causes, pathology, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of simple goitre.
Explain pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of toxic goitre and autoimmune or inflammatory thyroid disease.
Identify types, causes and management of benign thyroid neoplasms.
Discuss incidence, types, causes, pathology, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of malignant thyroid neoplasms and plan management of a solitary thyroid nodule.
Discuss pathogenesis, classifications, clinical presentations and management of hyperparathyroidism and hypoparathyroidism.
Discuss causes, classifications and pathogenesis of adrenal disorders and formulate a differential diagnosis for adrenal masses.
Discuss management of adrenal disorders, including adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and neuroblastoma.
Outline congenital anomalies of the breast and discuss pathology and management of traumatic fat necrosis.
Identify causes and clinical presentations of inflammatory breast disease and select diagnostic procedures and management approaches.
Describe types, pathogenesis, clinical presentations and management of fibrocystic breast disease and gynaecomastia.

Outline clinical presentation and management of phyllodes tumour and intraductal papilloma; classify breast cancer and discuss its incidence, risk factors, causes, clinical presentations, diagnosis, grading and management.
Design a plan for early detection of breast cancer in the community.
Understand differences between adult and paediatric surgery in surgical decisions, preoperative preparation, operative techniques and postoperative follow-up and management.
Explain incidence, causes, types, diagnosis and management of oesophageal atresia, tracheo-oesophageal fistula and oesophageal diverticulum.
Explain incidence, types, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis and duodenal atresia.
Discuss incidence, causes, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of Meckel diverticulum, intestinal atresia, malrotation, intussusception and necrotizing enterocolitis.
Discuss incidence, causes, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of anorectal congenital malformations and Hirschsprung disease.
Discuss incidence, diagnosis and management of biliary atresia and choledochal cyst.
Discuss classification, pathogenesis and management of haemangiomas and vascular malformations.
List types and causes of ischaemia and explain its pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis and management of aneurysms; plan management of arterial injuries and discuss pathogenesis and management of vasculitis.
List causes and classification of varicose veins.
Explain pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of varicose veins and outline management of venous ulcers.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
Outline classification, causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of lymphoedema.
Define burn injury, identify causes and explain burn pathogenesis.
Differentiate burn degrees by depth, healing pattern, clinical presentation, local management and complications.
Understand recent advances in local burn management and skin substitutes and discuss general and long-term multidisciplinary management of burned patients.
Design a health-education brochure for burn prevention and local management of burn injuries in the community.
Classify common skin and subcutaneous lesions and explain how to differentiate them.
Discuss aetiology, clinical presentations, complications and management of common skin and soft-tissue infections.
Discuss causes, types, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of sialadenitis, sialectasis, sialolithiasis, autoimmune salivary disease, salivary trauma and fistulae.
Outline classification of benign and malignant salivary tumours and discuss incidence, causes, pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management.
Classify jaw swellings and describe clinical and radiological findings of common jaw swellings.
Describe common surgical techniques used in management of jaw swellings.
Classify head and neck malignancies, explain clinical presentations and management, and identify types of block neck dissection.
Identify neck-trauma zones, describe mechanisms and clinical presentations, and design a management protocol for neck trauma.
Discuss management of facial and scalp soft-tissue trauma and clinical/radiological findings, classifications and principles of management of facial-bone fractures.
Describe classifications of congenital craniofacial clefts, multidisciplinary management, and indications, timing and principles of surgery.
Describe surgical anatomy of the hand and hand spaces.
Discuss clinical presentations and management of hand infections, diabetic hand, common hand swellings, hand tenosynovitis and Dupuytren contracture.
Define aesthetic surgery, identify common surgical and non-surgical techniques, and discuss indications and complications.
Categorize and differentiate urological complaints and identify different urological investigations, including commonly used radiological investigations.
Perform male and female urinary catheterization and explain indications and complications of catheterization.
Illustrate indications and techniques of suprapubic catheterization and nephrostomy tube placement.
Outline principles, indications and techniques of circumcision, post-circumcision complications, and medico-legal aspects of female circumcision.

Discuss aetiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of renal agenesis, pelvi-ureteric junction obstruction, vesicoureteral reflux, duplication, ectopic ureter, ureterocele, undescended testis, hypospadias, posterior urethral valve and exstrophy-epispadias complex.
Explain mechanisms, clinical presentation, diagnostic approach and management of urinary trauma, testicular torsion, penile fracture and priapism.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, clinical presentations, complications, diagnostic procedures and management of obstructive uropathy, urinary retention, anuria and haematuria.
Explain pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of pyelonephritis, renal abscess, cystitis, prostatitis and sexually transmitted diseases.
Discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, diagnosis and management of renal tumours and bladder cancer.
Explain theories, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of benign prostatic hyperplasia and discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, diagnosis and management of prostate cancer.
List causes, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of impotence and male infertility; identify penile prosthesis types and clinical presentation and management of varicocele.
Define voiding dysfunction, describe neurological bladder control and the micturition cycle, and classify voiding disorders.
Describe clinical presentations and management of urinary incontinence and nocturnal enuresis.
Explain urinary-stone aetiology and theories of formation, composition of common stones, clinical presentation, management options and recurrence prevention.
Explain mechanisms and types of chest trauma and illustrate clinical and radiological presentations; design a diagnostic and management plan.
Discuss aetiology, clinical presentation, radiological findings and complications of inflammatory lung and pleural conditions.
List benign and malignant lung tumours and discuss clinical presentations and radiological findings of lung neoplasms.
Describe indications, complications and principles of lung and pleural surgery.
Describe types of congenital heart disease and explain surgical principles of congenital heart surgery.
List valvular diseases and valve-replacement surgery; describe indications, limitations and techniques of coronary artery bypass; outline cardiac pacemakers and cardiopulmonary bypass.
Formulate differential diagnoses and outline diagnostic and management approaches for mediastinal masses.
Discuss causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of thoracic outlet syndrome.
Outline incidence, types, causes, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of Chiari malformation, Dandy–Walker malformation and dysraphism.
Define craniosynostosis and describe clinical presentations, types, causes, diagnosis and management.

Discuss mechanisms, types, causes, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of skull fractures, extradural haematoma, acute and chronic subdural haematoma, intraparenchymal injury and other extra-axial collections.
Explain mechanisms, causes, diagnosis and management of cervical-spine injuries, thoracolumbar-spine injuries and spinal-cord injury.
Outline incidence, causes, diagnosis and management of primary and metastatic brain tumours, cranial and peripheral nerve tumours, and spinal and spinal-cord tumours.
Explain causes, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of stroke, intracerebral haemorrhage, subarachnoid haemorrhage, venous sinus thrombosis and cerebral aneurysms.
Discuss causes, clinical presentation and management of hydrocephalus and describe mechanisms of cerebrospinal-fluid diversion.
Understand the importance of history taking in diagnosis of surgical diseases and take and record a structured patient-centred history.
Apply and present systematic abdominal examination and understand the pathogenesis of positive physical findings.
Understand the importance and scientific background of per-rectal examination and apply and interpret the examination.
Perform and present systematic clinical assessment of swellings.
Outline trauma types, define multiple-trauma patients, triage and causes of death in trauma, and describe management of life-threatening traumatic conditions.
Illustrate and apply recent trauma life-support guidelines.
Discuss diagnosis and management of crush syndrome and compartment syndromes and explain damage-control surgery and conservative management.
Understand patient health education regarding surgical options, side effects, complications, informed consent, photography, fasting, positioning and follow-up.

Discuss preoperative investigations and preparation, DVT-prophylaxis guidance, precautions for selected comorbidities/therapies, intraoperative precautions and management of common postoperative complications.
Understand scientific background, indications, complications and limitations of recent imaging techniques and common interventional radiology.
Understand laser theory, differentiate types of light therapies and describe indications, complications and limitations of phototherapy in surgery.
Define minimally invasive surgery and describe indications, common techniques, complications and limitations.
Identify basic surgical instruments, tubes and drains and describe indications, contraindications and complications.
Understand differences between suture types and suturing techniques, explain indications and apply common suturing techniques.
Define and classify causes of surgical jaundice, explain pathogenesis and diagnosis, and design a management plan.
Describe causes, clinical presentations and management of cholangitis.
Illustrate indications, advantages, disadvantages, side effects and complications of different abdominal incisions and describe their anatomical layers.
Perform and interpret thyroid examination and describe signs of thyrotoxicosis.
Discuss indications and types of thyroidectomy, explain operative steps and outline postoperative complications and their management.
Understand the importance and scientific background of routine breast examination and perform and interpret breast examination.
Formulate differential diagnoses of nipple discharge and explain management approaches.
Perform examination of distal pulses and describe symptoms and signs of acute and chronic ischaemia, varicose veins, DVT and post-phlebitic limb.
Define gangrene and its types, describe pathogenesis and management, explain indications for amputation, and recognize amputation levels and complications.
Define vascular access, describe indications and performance, and describe complications of different access types and their management.

Explain indications, techniques, complications and limitations of angiography and angioplasty; interpret arterial and venous angiograms; explain selective embolization and the role of angiography in trauma.
Identify diabetic foot and outline causes and management of diabetic-foot infections, including multidisciplinary care.
List types and indications of sympathectomy and illustrate techniques.
Discuss causes and pathogenesis of wounds, wound-healing mechanisms and factors, complications and abnormal healing, wound assessment, recent wound protocols and scar-management modalities.
Explain tissue-reconstruction aims and techniques, graft and flap definitions/classifications/indications/limitations, recent techniques and decision-making for tissue defects.
Explain pressure-ulcer pathogenesis and prevention, describe clinical grades and complications, and explain management.

Describe causes and clinical presentation of lymphadenopathy and management of lymphadenopathy and carcinoma of unknown primary; classify lymphomas and explain their presentation and the surgical role in diagnosis and management.
Describe neck triangles and differentiate common anterior and lateral neck swellings by clinical presentation and management.
Define and classify hernias, discuss clinical presentations and complications, outline management principles and recent abdominal-wall reconstruction principles.

Describe indications and types of mastectomy, conservative breast surgery and breast reconstruction, including precautions, timing and limitations; identify mammoplasty and mastopexy and describe surgical techniques for gynaecomastia.
Categorize and differentiate urological complaints and identify different urological and commonly used radiological investigations.
Perform male and female urinary catheterization; explain indications and complications and illustrate indications and techniques of suprapubic catheterization and nephrostomy.
Outline principles, indications and techniques of circumcision and post-circumcision complications and illustrate indications and medico-legal aspects of female circumcision.
Describe scientific background of chest radiology, indications and complications of chest-tube insertion, chest-tube mechanism and removal, and perform chest-tube insertion.
Discuss indications for thoracotomy and identify different types of thoracotomy.
Understand the scientific background of neurological examination and clinical signs and apply and interpret neurological examination.
Interpret plain X-rays, CT and MRI of the skull and spine.
Define acute abdomen, formulate its differential diagnosis and plan its management; classify gastrointestinal bleeding and design diagnostic and management plans.
Describe classifications and clinical presentations of gastrointestinal obstruction (paediatric/adult, acute/chronic, mechanical/functional) and demonstrate diagnosis and management.
Apply clinical tests to differentiate inguinal, inguinoscrotal and scrotal swellings.

Discuss aetiology, pathology, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of inguinoscrotal swellings and explain presentation and management of acute scrotum, testicular torsion, testicular trauma and inflammatory testicular conditions.

Explain causes, diagnosis and management of low-back pain, radiculopathy, cervical disc herniation, thoracic/lumbar degenerative disc disease, degenerative cervical disc disease, cervical myelopathy, adult spinal deformity and degenerative scoliosis.
Describe clinical presentations of metastatic carcinoma and explain management of metastatic prostatic carcinoma.
Design guidelines for management of a bed-ridden patient.
Understand the scientific principles of research.
Understand the ethical aspects of research.
